seen.where: szukajwarchiwach.gov.pl units 28223835 (no. 128), 28223837 (130), 28223838 (131), 28223850 (143), leaves opened in Chrome at photos.szukajwarchiwach.gov.pl _mid size (663-800 px); sibling 28223836 (129) also opened
seen.extent: No. 128: 1 page, 19 lines of spaced single letters. No. 130: scans 2, 3, 5, 6 carry spaced letters (faint on 6), roughly 50 lines in all, beside clear French; scan 7 not opened. No. 131 (Wilno, 11 July 1757): scans 2-4, roughly 70 lines of run-on letters with 3-digit groups, inside clear Polish. No. 143 (3 Mar 1771?): scan 3, right page, about 22 lines of spaced letters and pairs, after clear French.
seen.cipher: Two systems on the leaves. 128, 130 and 143: spaced lower-case Roman letters with a few doubled forms, system not determined. 131: continuous letters mixed with 3-digit numbers (860, 900, 999, 865, 925, 940 ...). No decipherment is written on or between the lines of any of these leaves at this resolution. Archive titles: 131 "List nierozszyfrowany", 143 "częściowo szyfr nierozwiązany". Caution on 128: its cover has a pencil note that reads "Część listu szyfrem (rozwiązany)" at 800 px, and scan 3 holds two clear French pages, which could be plain parts or a solution; no. 129, catalogued "szyfr rozwiązany", has the same spaced-letter look and shows no interlinear on the leaf opened, so "solved" there may mean clear pages filed with it.

1580.key_check: No key tested. Solved sibling 135 (8 Feb 1766) uses 3-digit numbers with French between the lines, per the 2 Nov look, and may bear on the numbers in 131; the spaced-letter system of 128, 130 and 143 is not that system. A key rebuilt from siblings has not been tried.
1580.key_in_volume: Same series, not the same unit: interlinear siblings 135-142, 129 "szyfr rozwiązany", 132 "z rozwiązaniem szyfru". Not transcribed and not tested on these four.

Catalogue entry for AGAD 1/338/0/1/446 (Branicki to Potocki) is a different letter.

Two systems: consider splitting 131.

seen.cipher: Graphic-sign cipher (hand-made signs with a few Latin-like forms and crosses) written in runs and word-like groups, with some clear Polish words among them; the letter is signed with a hard-to-read name after a French subscription. (The cipher is on scan 3, not scan 4 as the 2 Nov note had it.)
